Dalmatians were bred to be carriage dogs, guarding carriages and running along with the horses. They're extremely energetic, so be prepared to spend at least an hour a day running him, either on a leash or with a tennis ball. They will literally go insane if you don't get them enough exercise - destroying the house, attacking people, all that. They do best if they have a very clear job to perform, even if it's just helping you get the mail.

They have a lot of health problems due to overbreeding (thanks, Disney!) so make sure you get him a good check-up. They're prone to a large number of respiratory, joint, and muscle issues.

They're extremely sensitive and will absolutely not respond to any kind of training that involves anger and frustration on your part. You almost have to make deals with them, rather than train them. He will tune into your moods and react accordingly, even more so than most dogs. They form incredibly strong bonds with their owners, and do not do well when they're rehomed. If yours is in that situation, be very gentle with him. They need to be with their people, so while you don't have to let him sleep on the bed, I would strenuously advise against any situation where he isn't a full member of the family.

They're the sweetest dogs in the world if you treat them right, though. I miss the breed a lot.
